title: 円相場、よぎる2年前の記憶　日銀会合後の介入に市場身構え
extracted_text:
外国為替市場で円の急変に身構える参加者が出てきた。よぎるのは2年前、短期間で2度に及んだ政府・日銀によるドル売り・円買い介入の記憶だ。27〜28日の金融政策決定会合やその後の米統計、中東情勢次第では、2年前の再現となる可能性もある。

「せっかくのゴールデンウイークだが、出勤になるかもしれない」。ある市場参加者はこぼす。

1ドル=160円で円の下落が止まっているのは口先介入が理由だ。片山さつき財務相は15日、米ワシントンでベッセント米財務長官と会談したとX（旧ツイッター）への投稿で明らかにした。為替を巡り「さらに連絡緊密化で一致」したという。

ただSMBC日興証券の丸山凜途シニア金利・為替ストラテジストは「口先介入が繰り返されれば相場の感度は下がる」と話す。次の手として、介入の前段階であるレートチェックや実弾介入が想定される。

市場参加者は連休前後の日程に気をもむ。4月28日は日銀の金融政策決定会合後に植田和男総裁の記者会見、5月上旬には米金融政策の方向を占う米経済統計の発表が予定されている。計9.7兆円のドル売り・円買い介入に踏み切った2年前の4〜5月と重なる面が多い。

24年は4月26日、金融政策決定会合後の会見で植田総裁の発言が円安を容認したととらえられ、円安・ドル高に弾みがついた。

米側の要因も重なった。同日発表の米個人消費支出（PCE）物価指数が市場予想を上回り金融引き締めの長期化が意識され、ドル買いがさらに進んだ。

日本が休日の週明け29日に円相場が1ドル=160円にタッチ。ここで、1回目の介入が入った。

二の矢も放たれた。5月1日の米連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）後の記者会見でパウエル議長は次の政策変更が利上げになる可能性を「低い」と指摘。利下げ期待が浮上してドルが下落しはじめたところで再び政府・日銀の介入となった。結局円は一時151円台後半まで上昇し、1週間で8円の値幅が出た。

今回はどうか。まず日銀の4月利上げ観測は後退が続く。翌日物金利スワップ（OIS）市場が織り込む利上げ確率は月初に7割だったが、16日夕方時点では2割程度となった。

日銀は需給ギャップの再計算など、利上げに向けた地ならしをしてきたように市場に映る。中東情勢の影響が不透明で日銀が利上げを見送り「会見などで目先もなさそうと市場が受け止めれば、円安が数円進んでもおかしくない」（松井証券の鈴木翔マーケットアナリスト）。

米利上げ観測が浮上する可能性もある。米国では5月1日に米サプライマネジメント協会（ISM）製造業景況感指数、8日には雇用統計の発表が控える。三菱UFJモルガン・スタンレー証券の植野大作チーフ為替ストラテジストは「強い統計が出て利上げ観測が高まると、ドル買い主導で160円を超える可能性がある」と指摘する。

対ドル以外ではすでに金融政策を巡る思惑が反映されている。市場が利上げを見込むユーロや豪ドルに対し、円は歴史的な安値圏にある。

中東情勢も気がかりだ。米イランは停戦期間の再延長で合意したと伝わったが、交渉が不調となり原油高がドル買いを招くリスクはある。

介入が必要になった場合の手法に注目する声もある。 あおぞら銀行 の諸我晃チーフ・マーケット・ストラテジストは「米側の協力がちらつけば相場の方向性は変わるかもしれない」と指摘する。1月のレートチェックは米側が実施した。

こんな見方が出るのは、通常の介入では円安トレンドが変わらないとの見方が根強いからこそだ。

米商品先物取引委員会（CFTC）によると、ヘッジファンドなど非商業部門（投機筋）のドルに対する円の売り越し幅は7日時点で9.3万枚（1兆1717億円）。24年4月時点（17.9万枚）の半分だ。介入が投機筋の買い戻しを巻き込んで円高に持っていく力は当時に比べ小さい。

実需のドル買いの強さも違う。ニューヨーク原油先物はイラン攻撃前よりなお4割高い。輸入によるドル買い・円売りが出やすい。

介入はあるのか。あるとして、どんな手段か。重要日程を横目に、気の抜けない連休になりそうだ。

（坂部能生）

translated_text:
Participants in the foreign exchange market are bracing for potential sharp yen movements. What comes to mind is the memory of government and Bank of Japan dollar-selling, yen-buying interventions that occurred twice in a short period, roughly two years ago. Depending on the April 27-28 financial policy decision meeting and subsequent US statistics or Middle East developments, there is a possibility the two-year-ago scenario could repeat.

"It could be a golden week, but I might end up having to work," one market participant grumbles.

The yen's decline stopping at 1 dollar = 160 yen is due to verbal intervention. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama revealed on X (formerly Twitter) on the 15th that she met with US Treasury Secretary Bessent in Washington. Regarding the exchange rate, they agreed to further strengthen communication and cooperation.

However, SMBC Nikko Securities Senior Interest Rate and FX Strategist Rintaro Maruyama says, "If verbal intervention is repeated, the market's sensitivity to it decreases." As the next step, rate checks or actual intervention - the precursors to intervention - are being considered.

Market participants are anxious about the schedule around the consecutive holidays. April 28 features a press conference by Governor Kazuo Ueda following the BOJ's monetary policy decision meeting, and early May sees the release of US economic statistics that will provide clues about US monetary policy direction. This overlaps considerably with April-May two years ago when the government and BOJ carried out dollar-selling, yen-buying interventions totaling 9.7 trillion yen.

On April 26, 2024, remarks by Governor Ueda at the press conference following the monetary policy decision meeting were interpreted as accepting yen weakness, giving further momentum to yen depreciation and dollar appreciation.

US-side factors also aligned. On the same day, the US personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index released exceeded market expectations, raising awareness of prolonged monetary tightening, leading to further dollar buying.

On the Monday after Japan's holiday, April 29, the yen rate touched 1 dollar = 160 yen. This is when the first intervention occurred.

A second arrow was also launched. Following the May 1 US Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) press conference, Chair Powell noted that the next policy change being a rate hike was "low" probability. As rate cut expectations began to surface and the dollar started to fall, the government and BOJ intervened again. Ultimately, the yen temporarily rose to the low 151 yen range, an 8-yen movement in one week.

How about this time? First, expectations for a BOJ rate hike in April continue to recede. The probability of a rate hike factored in by the overnight index swap (OIS) market was 70% at the beginning of the month, but fell to around 20% by the evening of the 16th.

The BOJ appears to have been preparing the ground for a rate hike by recalculating the output gap, among other things. "If the market interprets that the BOJ will postpone a rate hike and that there seems to be no chance of meaningful action in press conferences or elsewhere due to unclear Middle East developments, it wouldn't be surprising if the yen depreciates by several yen," says Sho Suzuki, Market Analyst at Matsui Securities.

There is also a possibility of US rate hike expectations surfacing. On May 1 in the US, the Institute for Supply Management (ISM) manufacturing index is scheduled for release, and on the 8th, the employment statistics. Daisaku Ueno, Chief FX Strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities, notes, "If strong statistics emerge and rate hike expectations rise, there is a possibility of breaking 160 yen driven by dollar buying."

Regarding currencies other than the dollar, speculation about monetary policy is already being reflected. While the market expects rate hikes for the euro and Australian dollar, the yen is at historically low levels.

The Middle East situation is also concerning. While it was reported that the US and Iran agreed to extend the ceasefire period, negotiations collapsed, creating a risk of higher crude oil prices driving dollar buying.


There are also voices focusing on the approach should intervention become necessary. Aozora Bank Chief Market Strategist Akira Shoga points out, "If there is cooperation from the US side, the market direction could change." The January rate check was conducted by the US side.


Such views emerge precisely because there is a strong belief that regular intervention does not change the yen depreciation trend.


According to the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), the net short position of non-commercial sectors (speculators) such as hedge funds against the yen as of the 7th was 93,000 contracts (1.1717 trillion yen). This is half the level of April 2024 (179,000 contracts). Compared to that time, the power of intervention to drive yen appreciation by triggering speculative covering is smaller.

The strength of dollar buying for actual demand is also different. New York crude oil futures remain 40% higher than before the Iran attack. Dollar buying and yen selling through imports are likely.


Will there be intervention? If so, what methods will be used? It seems to be a holiday period where one cannot let their guard down, with important dates to watch.


(Sekine Yoshio)
title_en: Yen Rate Memories of Two Years Ago Resurface -- Market Braces for Intervention After BOJ Meeting
